title: The Defender Portal, Notifications and Alert Correlation

header.html: 1. Manage a security operations environment (40 to 45%)

Configure automation for Microsoft Defender XDR and Microsoft Sentinel: configure email notifications in Defender XDR, including incidents, actions and threat analytics; configure alert notifications in Defender XDR, including tuning, suppression and correlation
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

toc.title: How alerts become incidents: correlation and merging
Microsoft Sentinel in the Defender portal

html:
1One portal, one incident queue

The Microsoft Defender portal is where an analyst triages. Alerts from every Defender workload, and from Microsoft Sentinel once it is onboarded, are correlated into incidents in one queue.

Item Fact
Portal path Investigation & response > Incidents & alerts > Incidents
Alert One detection from one product
Incident A set of correlated alerts, the affected assets, investigations and evidence
Incident status Active (default), In progress, Resolved
Severity High, Medium, Low, Informational (starts at the highest alert severity)
Owner One user or group per incident
Exam tip

. The unit of work is the incident, not the alert. Defender places each alert into a new or an existing incident by its own correlation logic.

2Email notifications

Path: Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > General > Email notifications. Three tabs: Incidents, Actions, Threat analytics. You need the Manage security settings permission (basic permissions: Security Administrator or higher).

Tab What the rule filters Key options
Incidents Alert severity and device group scope Send only one notification per incident; include the organization name; include a tenant-specific portal link
Actions Action source (manual, automated), the actions, device groups (all or selected), action status (completed, failed) Not supported for custom detections that contain response actions
Threat analytics All reports, or by report type or tag At least one recipient

The incident wizard has five steps: Basics, Notification settings, Recipients (with Send test email), Review rule, Create rule.

Exam tip

. Actions notifications tell you when an automated or manual response action completed or failed. Incidents notifications tell you a new incident of a given severity exists. Pick the tab by the event.

3How alerts become incidents: correlation and merging

Rule Detail
Correlation Defender adds an alert to a new or existing incident by proprietary correlation logic
Merge The source incident moves into the target; the source is closed and tagged Redirected
Manual merge Five incidents at a time
Not merged when The source is closed; the assignees differ; the classifications or determinations differ; an entity limit would be exceeded; devices sit in different device groups (only when scoped device group correlation is on)

The advanced feature Restrict correlation to within scoped device groups (Module 2) stops incidents from combining devices of different device groups; it affects future correlation only.

Exam tip

. Different owners or different classifications block a merge. Align them first, then merge.

4Alert tuning and suppression

Tool Where Effect
Alert suppression rule (Defender for Endpoint) Settings > Endpoints > Rules > Alert suppression Suppresses matching alerts (for example a known-good line-of-business app); you can turn on, edit or delete the rule
Edit a suppression rule Same page You can release alerts already suppressed
Defender for Identity tuning Alert tuning rules (Defender format) Replaces the old Excluded entities setting of the classic format

Suppress only proven false positives. A rule hides future alerts, so a wide rule can hide a real attack.

Exam tip

. A noisy alert from a trusted internal tool is solved with a suppression or tuning rule scoped to that tool, not by turning the detection off.

5Microsoft Sentinel in the Defender portal

After onboarding, Sentinel works inside the Defender portal. Azure portal support ends after March 31, 2027. The move has no extra cost.

Azure portal item Defender portal location
Incidents Investigation & response > Incidents & alerts > Incidents
Logs Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting
Workbooks, Hunting, Notebooks, MITRE ATT&CK Microsoft Sentinel > Threat management
Content hub Microsoft Sentinel > Content management
Data connectors, Analytics, Watchlists, Automation Microsoft Sentinel > Configuration
Threat intelligence Threat intelligence > Intel management
Settings System > Settings > Microsoft Sentinel

Differences that the exam may test: the incident queue is unified; Fusion is disabled; Microsoft incident creation rules are not supported; incidents created by API, playbook or by hand in Azure do not sync to Defender; a closed incident is not reopened by a new alert; bookmarks are not in Advanced hunting.

Exam tip

. Analytics rules and automation live under Microsoft Sentinel > Configuration in the Defender portal.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A SOC manager wants one email per incident whenever a high-severity incident is created, even if several alerts join it later. Which setting meets the requirement?

  • AAn Actions notification rule with the action source set to automated
  • BAn Incidents notification rule with one notification per incident enabled
  • CA Threat analytics notification rule that covers all report types
  • DAn Incidents notification rule that sends an email for every alert
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Incidents tab filters by severity and has the option to send only one notification per incident.

S2The team wants an email when an automated device action fails to complete. Which notification tab should be used?

  • AThe Incidents tab, with the alert severity set to high only
  • BThe Threat analytics tab, with a rule for all reports
  • CThe Actions tab, with manual as the source and completed as the status
  • DThe Actions tab, with automated as the source and failed as the status
Show the answer

Answer: D. Actions rules filter by source and by completed or failed status.

S3An analyst wants to be told whenever new ransomware reports appear in threat analytics. What should be configured?

  • AA Threat analytics notification rule filtered by report type or tag
  • BAn Incidents notification rule filtered to high severity alerts only
  • CAn Actions notification rule that includes all response actions
  • DAn alert suppression rule that releases ransomware alerts
Show the answer

Answer: A. Threat analytics rules can cover all reports or filter by report type or tag.

S4An analyst merges two incidents, but the merge is refused. One incident is assigned to a user and the other is assigned to a different user. What is the reason?

  • AIncidents can be merged only once in a single day
  • BIncidents with different assignees are not merged
  • CIncidents from different products can never be merged
  • DIncidents with the same severity are merged by the system
Show the answer

Answer: B. Different assignees, different classifications or determinations, or a closed source incident block the merge.

S5A Sentinel engineer who used the Azure portal needs to open the analytics rules after onboarding to the Defender portal. Where are they?

  • AInvestigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting
  • BMicrosoft Sentinel > Threat management > Hunting
  • CSystem > Settings > Microsoft Sentinel > Workbooks
  • DMicrosoft Sentinel > Configuration > Analytics
Show the answer

Answer: D. Data connectors, Analytics, Watchlists and Automation are under Microsoft Sentinel > Configuration.

S6A user must create email notification rules but must hold the lowest role that allows it. Which permission is required?

  • AGlobal Administrator, which is the only role allowed to do so
  • BSecurity Reader, which allows rules to be viewed and created
  • CManage security data, held only by Microsoft Sentinel Reader
  • DManage security settings, for example through Security Administrator
Show the answer

Answer: D. Email notification rules need the Manage security settings permission.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does the Actions notification tab report?

Show the answer

Manual or automated response actions that completed or failed.

R2What happens to the source incident after a merge?

Show the answer

It is closed and tagged Redirected.

R3How many incidents can be merged manually at a time?

Show the answer

Five.

R4Where do you manage alert suppression rules for Defender for Endpoint?

Show the answer

Settings > Endpoints > Rules > Alert suppression.

R5When does Azure portal support for Microsoft Sentinel end?

Show the answer

After March 31, 2027.

R6Which Defender for Identity feature replaced the Excluded entities setting in the Defender format?

Show the answer

Alert tuning rules.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Queue Investigation & response > Incidents & alerts > Incidents
Notifications Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > General > Email notifications: Incidents, Actions, Threat analytics
Permission Manage security settings (Security Administrator or higher)
Merge blockers closed source, different assignees, different classification, entity limit, different device groups
Suppression Settings > Endpoints > Rules > Alert suppression
Sentinel paths Configuration (analytics, connectors, automation), Threat management (hunting, workbooks)
